head: 8ac940ff581aa344ab8f859874f6d4c0ecaec6b6

source.ref: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59322; AACR-Bench dataset.json rows 976, 977, 978, 979, 980, forbid seed row 1942; licence MIT read from LICENSE.txt and the touched file's header at head; hand-checked 2026-10-23 by vetter A; the pull request's later commit a046b3fa0d (merged 2025-01-08 as dba6cd892d) replaced the pool rental with stackalloc for up to 32 purposes

rationale: A performance rewrite of the additional authenticated data template behind NET10_0_OR_GREATER; the new bytes match the old BinaryWriter output, so no candidate names a real defect. stackalloc-lengths (row 979, a person's) is true at head and upstream adopted it in the same pull request (author-fix), but it is a micro-optimization in protector construction, which the pull request itself says is not a hot path, so it is optional. Dropped: row 976 (a person's) because the BitOperations and span GetBytes code is compiled only for net10.0 at head, and a missing API would be a compiler error anyway; row 977 because every production caller rejects a null purpose and the old code threw on null too; row 978 because purposes are chosen by the application, overflow needs gigabytes of purpose text, and span writes are bounds-checked, so at worst it throws; row 980 because an unreturned pooled array is only garbage-collected and upstream kept no try/finally. Forbid: seed row 1942 suggests the write index can run past the buffer, but both lengths come from the same encoding over the same immutable strings and every write goes through a bounds-checked slice.

expect.concern: Every template construction rents and returns an ArrayPool buffer just to hold a few purpose lengths, an overhead a stackalloc with a pool fallback for large purpose counts would avoid.

forbid.reason: The write index cannot pass the buffer end: the buffer is sized from GetByteCount over the same strings with the same encoding, and each write goes through a bounds-checked span slice, so a mismatch would throw rather than overrun.
